Analyze the MFRM design network

Source: R/api-reports.R
mfrm_network_analysis.Rd

Analyze the MFRM design network

Usage

mfrm_network_analysis(
  fit = NULL,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  top_n_subsets = NULL,
  min_observations = 0,
  include_graph = FALSE,
  data = NULL,
  person = NULL,
  facets = NULL,
  score = NULL,
  basis = c("observed", "planned"),
  weight = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional output from diagnose_mfrm().

top_n_subsets

Optional maximum number of connected-subset rows to retain before constructing the graph.

min_observations

Minimum observations required to keep a subset row.

include_graph

Logical; if TRUE, include the underlying igraph object in the returned bundle. Defaults to FALSE so outputs remain easy to serialize.

data

Optional raw assignment/rating data, supplied instead of fit.

person, facets

Names of the person column and one or more facet columns in data. Include only Rater in facets to inspect person-rater links without a common Criterion node obscuring separate panels.

score

Numeric score column for basis = "observed". Recode study-specific missing markers to NA first; no category recoding or estimation is done.

basis

"observed" includes rows with complete identifiers and nonmissing finite scores; "planned" includes complete assignment rows without scores. Planned networks require score = NULL and weight = NULL.

weight

Optional numeric weight column for observed raw data. Missing and zero-weight rows do not create edges. Edge weights still count rows, not sampling weights. Negative or infinite weights are refused.

Value

A bundle of class mfrm_network_analysis containing:

  • summary: graph-level connectedness and vulnerability metrics

  • node_metrics: node-level degree, strength, graph-theoretic centrality, and cutpoint flags

  • edge_metrics: edge-level weights, betweenness, and bridge flags

  • facet_summary: facet-level aggregation of node/bridge indicators

  • cut_nodes: articulation-point rows from node_metrics

  • bridge_edges: bridge rows from edge_metrics

Details

Nodes are Person or facet levels; undirected edges join levels appearing in the same rating, weighted by co-observation counts. This assignment graph reveals disconnected components, not ability or rater quality. Connectedness alone does not establish model identification. For score relationships instead, use rater_network_analysis() or rater_halo_network_analysis().

SourceSubsets, RetainedSubsets and ScopeComplete record whether subset filters retained the full observed design. Connectedness of selected subsets cannot be generalized to omitted subsets. Recreate older design reviews from the existing fit and matching diagnostics to record this coverage. plot(net, type = "centrality"), plot(net, type = "facet_summary"), and plot(net, type = "network") provide immediate visual checks; use draw = FALSE to return a ggplot without drawing, then plot_data() to extract its reusable data.

Reading the graph

  • Components: more than one component means separate co-observation regions, including known levels without observed links.

  • IsArticulationPoint: a node whose removal would increase disconnectedness.

  • IsBridge: an edge whose removal would increase disconnectedness.

  • Betweenness: a routing-dependence indicator; high values identify levels that carry many shortest paths through the design graph.

References

  • McEwen, M. R. (2015). Development of a Software Prototype for Generating and Classifying Incomplete Many-Facet-Rasch Model Rating Designs. Brigham Young University.

  • Csardi, G., Nepusz, T., Traag, V., Horvat, S., Zanini, F., Noom, D., & Muller, K. (2026). igraph: Network Analysis and Visualization.

Before fitting

Supply data, person, facets and score for a prefit graph, or use basis = "planned" for an assignment roster. Observed-only data cannot reveal absent assignments; a fit supplies only retained rows. Graph connectivity is not full model identification, and filtering does not establish linking. See "Before fitting" in subset_connectivity_report() for unscored/isolate rows, the inclusion audit and source versus retained component counts.

See also

subset_connectivity_report(), diagnose_mfrm(), mfrmr_linking_and_dff, mfrmr_visual_diagnostics

Examples

# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("mfrm_network_analysis", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {
  net <- mfrm_network_analysis(data = ratings, person = "Person",
    facets = "Rater", score = "Score")
  net$summary
  plot(net, type = "network", draw = FALSE)
}
} # }
